calls.thesis: Adding all the way down; bought from $1,800 two years ago, now in the $1,400s; DCF fair value ~$2,000 on conservative 20% EBIT growth and 25x exit EBIT (22.4% CAGR); revenue +45% YoY, ~$38.5B TTM vs $3.3B in Nov 2020 at the same price; Brazil real headwind but growth held through the prior devaluation.

First tracked MELI call. Added to his position after the 12.4% post-earnings drop to near 52-week lows (~$1,500, ~$76bn market cap): revenue +45% (+41% FX-neutral), TPV +53%, GMV +38%, Brazil accelerating +50%, fintech 93m MAU +29%, credit book +62%, ads +51% and taking share; margins are being deliberately sacrificed to compound, and he estimates the business already earns ~$6bn of underlying profit (~13x). A 5-10-20 year hold; short-term volatility irrelevant.
calls.price_at_call: ~$1,500 (down 12.4% on the day, near 52-week lows; ~$76bn market cap)
calls.base_case: Growth stays 20%+ and margins expand once investment slows; profits explode as the credit/advertising flywheel matures.
calls.bull_case: In 5 years revenue is multiples higher and the stock is far above $1,500 as LatAm digitisation compounds.
calls.bear_case: Margins never expand, Mexico deceleration spreads, or 90+ day NPLs (uptrending ~19.3%) deteriorate into real credit losses.
